argument_summary: The locked certification decision should not be defended as cleanly compliant on the present record. The admissible support is narrower: aggregate readiness cleared by 2.2 percentage points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the rollout is limited to 8% with rollback capability, which makes certification a weak but supportable deployment decision when paired with explicit documentation of the exposed limitation. The better interpretation is not that rollout controls cure the issue, but that they reduce operational risk while the packet preserves the unresolved fraud dispute review limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: Treating the current record as requiring immediate escalation to a stronger adverse conclusion would overstate the operational risk evidence. The admissible record shows aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a reversible 8% rollout, so the remaining dispute is about governance treatment of a known exposed limitation, not an uncontrolled launch condition. A bounded caveat is better aligned to the actual record than assuming the entire certification basis fails.
claims_about_policy: The policy record cuts both ways. It does not permit treating small-percentage rollout, monitoring, or rollback as a substitute for disclosure when the affected fraud dispute review use case remains exposed. At the same time, the policy framework allows deployment to be defended on a caveated basis when the limitation is expressly documented rather than denied. On the admissible record, certification is therefore supportable only as caveated compliance tied to disclosure of the material limitation, not as full compliance established by rollout controls alone.
concessions: The fraud dispute review segment is below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the fraud dispute review exposure.
There is no admissible evidence in this record that the required disclosure was completed before launch.
Rollout controls and monitoring are supportive but not sufficient, by themselves, under the policy text.
